Inverse Galois problem

Words: 131 Articles: 1
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
The inverse Galois problem asks which finite groups occur as Galois groups over a given field, with the classical problem taking the base field to be Q. A regular realization over K(T) and Galois-preserving Hilbert specialization solve an instance over a Hilbertian field. Realization over an algebraically closed constant field's rational function field alone does not supply descent to Q.

Rigid ramification type (Ni(G;C1​,…,Cr​)/G)

Words: 77
Inverse Galois problem OurBigBook.com
Fix ordered branch positions and conjugacy classes Ci​ in a finite group G. The generating product-one tuples (g1​,…,gr​)∈∏Ci​ form the inner Nielsen set. The type is rigid when this set is nonempty and a single simultaneous-conjugation orbit. Over C(T) this fixes the connected Galois cover up to isomorphism: tuples prescribe the monodromy epimorphism of the punctured sphere, and conjugate epimorphisms give isomorphic covers; the local completions at punctures are uniquely determined by their cyclic monodromy.

Compact Galois module

Words: 45
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
A compact Galois module is a compact profinite abelian group equipped with a continuous Galois group action. An abelian pro-p group is naturally a compact Zp​-module. A continuous action of the Galois group of a Zp-extension extends to its Iwasawa algebra of a Zp-extension. This compact topology differs from the discrete topology usually used in Galois cohomology.

Solvable field extension

Words: 40
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
A finite separable extension is solvable when its normal closure has a solvable group as Galois group. In characteristic zero it is contained in a radical tower after adjoining suitable roots of unity; containment need not mean it is itself a tower of radical adjunctions.

Radical extension

Words: 54
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
In the strict tower convention, a radical extension is a field obtained through finitely many adjunctions aini​​∈Ki−1​, Ki​=Ki−1​(ai​). Some texts instead use the term for any subfield of such a tower. This distinction matters: solvability by radicals implies containment in a tower, and need not give a radical tower entirely inside the original field.

Absolute Galois group (GK​=Gal(Ksep/K))

Words: 37
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
The absolute Galois group of a field K is GK​=Gal(Ksep/K). It is a profinite group, the inverse limit of the Galois groups of finite Galois extensions. Its continuous actions on discrete modules are the coefficients for Galois cohomology.

Galois closure of a field extension (M/K)

Words: 46
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
The Galois closure of a finite separable extension L/K is the smallest Galois extension in a fixed separable closure containing L. It is generated by all the conjugates of L. If G=Gal(M/K) and H=Gal(M/L), their subgroup core is trivial. This is distinct from the existing group-theoretic normal closure.

Fundamental theorem of Galois theory

Words: 21
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
For a finite Galois extension L/K, intermediate fields correspond inclusion-reversingly to subgroups of Gal(L/K). Normal subgroups correspond to Galois intermediate extensions.

Kummer theory

Words: 594 Articles: 10
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
When a field K contains the nth roots of unity and its characteristic does not divide n, Kummer theory identifies cyclic extensions of degree dividing n with suitable classes in K×/(K×)n. Cohomologically,
H1(GK​,μn​)≃K×/(K×)n.
(1)

Finite ramification support for radical extensions (S=S∞​∪{v:v(n)>0}∪{v:v(a)≡0(modn) for some [a]∈Δ})

Words: 80
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
For a number field and finite subgroup Δ⊂K∗/K∗n, adjoining all the indicated nth roots gives an extension unramified outside the displayed finite set. The valuations modulo n are independent of representatives. At a finite place outside S, divide each radicand by a local nth power of a uniformizer to obtain a unit. Its polynomial has separable reduction because n is invertible. A finite unramified extension containing all residue roots contains all lifted roots by Hensel's lemma. This proof does not require μn​⊂K.

Cyclic Galois resolvent (R(w)=∑j=0m−1​ζ−jgj(w))

Words: 99
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
For a cyclic Galois extension M/K of degree m, choose a generator g and a primitive mth root of unity ζ∈K. Reindexing the displayed sum gives gR(w)=ζR(w). Linear independence of distinct field embeddings ensures this sum is not identically zero as a function of w. Choosing α=R(w)=0 therefore gives m distinct conjugates ζjα, while αm∈K. Consequently M=K(α) is the splitting field of Xm−αm. Independence follows by taking a shortest supposed linear relation among distinct automorphisms, evaluating at uv and subtracting a suitable multiple of the relation at v to remove one term but not all terms.

Kummer reflection in Iwasawa theory (Xχ​∼Yωχ−1ι​(1))

Words: 56
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
For nontrivial even χ in the full cyclotomic tower of Q, Kummer theory relates the p-ramified Iwasawa module to the reflected odd unramified Iwasawa module, up to pseudo-isomorphism. Here ι(γ)=γ−1 and (1) is the Tate twist. The induced substitution on characteristic series is T↦u(1+T)−1−1, where u is the cyclotomic value of γ. Omitting either operation changes the interpolation convention.

Kummer cohomology divisibility criterion (Hn+1(L,μp​)=0)

Words: 48
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
When the characteristic differs from p, the Kummer sequence gives 0→Hn(L,Ks×​)/p→Hn+1(L,μp​)→Hn+1(L,Ks×​)[p]→0. For n≥1, the positive-degree multiplicative groups are torsion. Thus the middle group is zero exactly when the first multiplicative group is p-divisible and the second has zero p-primary torsion.

Unramified Kummer classes with bounded prime support (K(S,m)={[a]:vp​(a)≡0(modm) outside S})

Words: 64
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
For a number field K, a finite set S and m≥2, let K(S,m) consist of classes [a]∈K∗/K∗m whose valuations outside S are divisible by m. It fits into 0→OK,S×​/(OK,S×​)m→K(S,m)→Cl(OK,S​)[m]→0. The S-unit group is finitely generated and the ideal class group is finite, so K(S,m) is finite. When S contains primes dividing m, this controls unramified multiplicative Kummer classes outside S.

Square-class group of a field (K×/(K×)2)

Words: 176 Articles: 3
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
The square-class group identifies two nonzero elements of a field when their quotient is a square. Multiplication makes it an abelian group of exponent two, hence a vector space over F2​. It records quadratic extensions and the images of Kummer theory for n=2.

Square-class group of the 2-adic Gaussian field (Q2​(i)×/Q2​(i)×2≅C24​)

Words: 28
Square-class group of a field OurBigBook.com
The valuation contributes one factor C2​. The unit decomposition of the 2-adic Gaussian field contributes μ4​/μ42​≅C2​ and the additive quotient Z2​[i]/2Z2​[i]≅C22​. Thus there are sixteen square classes and fifteen quadratic extensions over this field.

Square class ([a]∈K∗/K∗2)

Words: 109 Articles: 1
Square-class group of a field OurBigBook.com
The square class of a∈K∗ is its image in the square-class group of a field K∗/K∗2. Two nonzero elements have the same square class exactly when their quotient is a square. Every element of this quotient has order dividing 2. Over the rational numbers, a square class has a unique signed squarefree integer representative.
Square-class group of a p-adic field (Qp×​/(Qp×​)2)
Words: 58
Square class OurBigBook.com
For odd p, parity of valuation and the square class of the unit residue give a group C2​×C2​, represented by 1,u,p,pu for a unit u with nonsquare residue. For p=2, valuation parity and unit residue modulo eight give C23​, with generators −1,5,2. The unit criteria follow from the Hensel lemma, using its strong derivative version for p=2.

Kummer extension

Words: 34
Kummer theory OurBigBook.com
When a field K contains the relevant roots of unity, adjoining an nth root of an element of K gives a Kummer extension. Such extensions describe abelian extensions of exponent dividing n.

Galois cohomology (Hi(G,M))

Words: 571 Articles: 9
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
Galois cohomology is the group cohomology of a Galois group acting on a module. For a discrete G-module M, the first group is the quotient of crossed homomorphisms c(στ)=c(σ)+σc(τ) by maps c(σ)=σm−m.

Weil–Châtelet group (WC(A/K)=H1(K,A))

Words: 100
Galois cohomology OurBigBook.com
For an abelian variety A over a field K, its Weil–Châtelet group is the Galois cohomology group H1(K,A(Ksep)), classifying torsors under A. Such an algebraic-group torsor becomes A after passing to a separable closure but need not have a K-point. A chosen geometric point identifies the torsor with A and its Galois descent with a cocycle; changing that point adds a coboundary. The zero class is precisely the torsor with a rational point. For an elliptic curve, these torsors are genus-one curves with a specified action and Jacobian. Over a number field the kernel of restriction to every completion is the Tate–Shafarevich group.

Galois descent of vector spaces (L⊗K​VG≅V)

Words: 139 Articles: 2
Galois cohomology OurBigBook.com
For a Finite Galois extension L/K and a finite-dimensional L-space V with a semilinear action of its Galois group, the map L⊗K​VG→V is an isomorphism. The vectors ∑σ​σ(a)σ(v) are invariant and span V by the Artin independence theorem. Choosing an invariant L-basis then identifies the invariant space with its K-span. The proof does not divide by the extension degree.

Descent classification of central simple algebras (CSAn​(L/K)≅H1(G,PGLn​(L)))

Words: 45
Galois descent of vector spaces OurBigBook.com
A splitting isomorphism of a central simple algebra with Mn​(L) transports its Galois action to Tσ​=cσ​σ0​, giving a nonabelian first cohomology class. Conversely a cocycle gives a semilinear algebra action whose invariants descend to a central simple algebra. Equivalent cocycles give isomorphic fixed algebras. This gives a pointed-set bijection CSAn​(L/K)≅H1(Gal(L/K),PGLn​(L)).

Semilinear action (σ(av)=σ(a)σ(v))

Words: 39
Galois descent of vector spaces OurBigBook.com
For an extension L/K with Galois group G, a semilinear action on an L-space is an additive group action satisfying σ(av)=σ(a)σ(v). Scalar coefficients are transformed along with vectors. Invariants form a K-space, and Galois descent of vector spaces reconstructs the original space from it.

First Galois cohomology unramified outside a finite set (HS1​(K,M))

Words: 71
Galois cohomology OurBigBook.com
For a finite Galois module M unramified outside a finite set S, define HS1​(K,M) as the classes in Galois cohomology whose restriction to inertia is zero at every finite prime outside S. This means zero as a cohomology class, rather than zero for every possible representative. Passing to a finite Galois extension on which M is constant reduces the finiteness problem to characters with bounded ramification and a finite restriction kernel.

Galois module

Words: 114 Articles: 1
Galois cohomology OurBigBook.com
A discrete Galois module over K is an abelian group with a continuous action of the absolute Galois group GK​. Continuity means that each element has an open stabilizer. Examples are the algebraic points of an elliptic curve, its finite torsion module E[m], and the group of roots of unity μm​. Galois cohomology takes continuous cocycles with values in such a module.

Galois module of roots of unity (μm​⊆Ks×​)

Words: 55
Galois module OurBigBook.com
The module μm​ consists of the mth roots of unity in a separable closure. If the field characteristic does not divide m, it has m elements and fits into the Kummer sequence 1→μm​→Ks×​m​Ks×​→1. Its Galois action is the cyclotomic action; a generator gives a noncanonical identification with Z/mZ.

Hilbert's theorem 90 (H1(K,K∗)=0)

Words: 112 Articles: 1
Galois cohomology OurBigBook.com
For a finite Galois extension L/K, multiplicative Hilbert theorem 90 says H1(Gal(L/K),L∗)=0. A multiplicative cocycle has the form cσ​=σ(b)/b. One proof forms a nonzero sum A=∑σ​cσ​σ(a), using linear independence of field automorphisms. Its transformation law is τA=cτ−1​A, so b=A−1 gives cτ​=τ(b)/b. Passing to the algebraic closure gives H1(K,K∗)=0, so the multiplicative Kummer sequence identifies H1(K,μm​) with K∗/K∗m.

Unit form of Hilbert theorem 90 (NL/K​(x)=1⟺x=ϕ(y)/y,y∈OL×​)

Words: 44
Hilbert's theorem 90 OurBigBook.com
For an unramified extension of non-Archimedean local fields, let ϕ generate its cyclic Galois group. The ordinary Hilbert theorem 90 supplies b∈L× with x=ϕ(b)/b. A common uniformizer π∈K gives y=π−vL​(b)b∈OL×​, retaining the same quotient because ϕ fixes π. The reverse implication follows by telescoping the field norm.

Words: 33
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
In a field of characteristic p>0, the Frobenius map x↦xp is an injective field endomorphism because
(x+y)p=xp+yp.
(2)

In characteristic p, the coefficient i in a formal derivative vanishes exactly when p divides i.

Polynomial with zero formal derivative in characteristic p

Words: 29
Formal derivative in positive characteristic OurBigBook.com
Over a field of characteristic p>0,
f′(T)=0⟺f(T)=g(Tp)

Separable polynomial

Words: 94 Articles: 2
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
A polynomial over a field is separable when it has no repeated root in a splitting field. Equivalently, it is coprime to its formal derivative.

Separability of roots of unity

Words: 32
Separable polynomial OurBigBook.com
If the characteristic of a field does not divide the positive integer m, then Xm−1 is separable. Its formal derivative is mXm−1, and a common root would have to be both nonzero and zero.

Irreducible polynomial in characteristic zero is separable

Words: 38
Separable polynomial OurBigBook.com
If f is irreducible over a field of characteristic zero, then f′=0 and degf′<degf. Thus f cannot divide f′, so irreducibility gives gcd(f,f′)=1. Consequently f has no repeated root in any extension field.

Automorphism-count divisibility theorem

Words: 31
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
For a finite extension K/F, the automorphism group G=AutF​(K) has order dividing [K:F]. Indeed, Artin's theorem gives [K:KG]=∣G∣, while F⊆KG and the tower law gives the divisibility.

Words: 37
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
Let L/K have degree d with gcd(d,n)=1. If a=xn∈K for some x∈L, then
ad=NL/K​(x)n.
(4)
Choosing r,s∈Z with rd+sn=1 gives
a=(NL/K​(x)ras)n,
(5)
so a was already an nth power in K.

Algebraic element

Words: 57 Articles: 1
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
An element α of a field extension L/K is algebraic over K when some nonzero polynomial in K[X] vanishes at α.

Minimal polynomial of an algebraic element (mα,K​(X))

Words: 35
Algebraic element OurBigBook.com
The minimal polynomial of an algebraic element α over K is the unique monic polynomial of least positive degree in K[X] that vanishes at α. It is irreducible, and its degree equals [K(α):K].

Primitive element of a field extension

Words: 96 Articles: 1
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
A primitive element of a finite extension L/K is an element α∈L such that L=K(α).
The primitive element theorem proves existence under finite separability; the primitive element of a field extension is the generator whose existence the theorem asserts.

Primitive elements form a principal Zariski-open set

Words: 64
Primitive element of a field extension OurBigBook.com
Fix a K-basis of a finite extension L/K of degree n. The coordinates of 1,α,…,αn−1 are polynomial functions of the coordinates of α, because multiplication in L has fixed structure constants. The determinant D(α) of those coordinate columns is therefore a polynomial, and
K[α]=L⟺D(α)=0.
(6)
Thus the primitive-element locus is the distinguished Zariski-open set D(D)⊆AKn​, possibly empty for a non-simple extension.

Primitive element theorem

Words: 53 Articles: 1
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
Every finite separable extension L/K is generated by one element: L=K(α) for some α∈L.

Purely inseparable extension without a primitive element

Words: 37
Primitive element theorem OurBigBook.com
Let K=Fp​(s,t) and L=K(s1/p,t1/p) for algebraically independent s,t. The p2 monomials si/ptj/p with 0≤i,j<p form a basis, whereas every α∈L satisfies αp∈K. Thus [L:K]=p2 but [K(α):K]≤p, so no primitive element of a field extension exists.

Finite separable simple extension implications

Words: 46
Galois theory OurBigBook.com
A finite separable extension is simple by the primitive element theorem. A simple separable extension is finite because its generator is separable and hence algebraic. Finite and simple does not imply separable: in characteristic p, Fp​(t1/p)/Fp​(t) is finite and simple but purely inseparable.

If a,b,ab are nonsquares in a field K of characteristic other than two, then
K(a​,b​)/K
(7)

Unramified biquadratic extension of a real quadratic field (Q(p​,q​)/Q(pq​))

Words: 138
Biquadratic extension OurBigBook.com
For distinct primes p,q≡1(mod4), put E=Q(p​,q​) and K=Q(pq​). Dihedral fixed field in one rational variable (C(z)D2n​=C(zn+z−n))

Words: 73
Fixed field OurBigBook.com
Automorphisms σ(z)=ζn​z and τ(z)=1/z generate a dihedral group of order 2n. The invariant w=zn+z−n has rational map degree 2n, so [C(z):C(w)]=2n. The fixed-field theorem for a finite automorphism group gives the same degree over its fixed field, proving equality. For odd prime n, the nontrivial proper subgroups are the rotation group and the n reflection groups. Their fixed fields are C(zn) and C(z+ζn−j​/z) for reflections σjτ, respectively.

Dihedral fixed field of a two-variable rational function field

Words: 63
Fixed field OurBigBook.com
On K=Q(x,y), let σ(x,y)=(y,−x) and τ(x,y)=(x,−y). They generate a dihedral group of order eight, and
K⟨σ,τ⟩=Q(x2+y2,x2y2).
(36)
The inclusion from right to left is immediate. In the other direction, x2,y2 solve a quadratic over the displayed field and adjoining their square roots has degree at most four; the resulting total degree is at most eight, while the automorphism-count bound for a finite field extension gives the reverse bound.

Galois theory OurBigBook.com
If a finite group G acts faithfully by automorphisms on a field L, then L/LG is Galois, has degree ∣G∣, and has Galois group G.
This theorem constructs a Galois extension from a finite group of field automorphisms; it is not an alternative name for the extension itself.

Let an automorphism σ of an algebraically closed field L have finite order and fixed field K. Artin's fixed-field theorem makes L/K finite cyclic Galois. Galois theory OurBigBook.com
For a monic polynomial with roots ri​, its discriminant is ∏i<j​(ri​−rj​)2 and vanishes exactly for a repeated root.

Squarefree polynomial discriminant does not imply irreducibility

Words: 95
Polynomial discriminant OurBigBook.com
A squarefree polynomial discriminant does not ensure that the polynomial defines a field of its stated degree. For example, x3−2x−1=(x+1)(x2−x−1) has discriminant five. Its roots have degrees one or two, so no root generates a cubic number field. In particular 1,α,α2 cannot be a field basis for any of its roots. The squarefree discriminant certifies an integral basis argument assumes that the polynomial is the minimal polynomial: then the discriminant of its power basis is the field discriminant times the square of the order index. For a reducible squarefree polynomial the analogous rank belongs instead to its quotient algebra, which is a product of fields, not to one root field.

Words: 98 Articles: 1

For a depressed quartic x4+px2+qx+r with roots α1​,…,α4​, the three pair-partition quantities α1​α2​+α3​α4​ and its two analogues are the roots of
y3−py2−4ry+(4pr−q2).
(42)
The Galois action on these roots is the quotient of its action on the four quartic roots by the Klein four-group.

S4 criterion from the cubic resolvent of an irreducible quartic

Words: 55
Cubic resolvent of a quartic OurBigBook.com
If an irreducible quartic over a field of characteristic zero has a cubic resolvent of a quartic whose Galois group of a polynomial is S3​, then the quartic has Galois group S4​. Irreducibility places the quartic group among the transitive subgroups of the symmetric group on four points, while the action on its three root pairings is surjective onto S3​. Of the possibilities C4​,V4​,D8​,A4​,S4​, only S4​ has this image.

Evaluating arbitrary monic polynomials of successive degrees 0,…,m−1 gives the same determinant as evaluating the monomials of those degrees. The basis-change matrix is triangular with diagonal entries one, so its determinant is one. This permits an orthogonal polynomial basis to replace the monomials in eigenvalue densities.

Words: 67
Vandermonde determinant OurBigBook.com
The left side is an alternating polynomial of total degree one more than Δ(x). Dividing by the Vandermonde determinant gives a symmetric homogeneous polynomial of degree one, necessarily a∑i​xi​+bt. At t=0, a=1; differentiation in t and the Euler theorem for homogeneous functions give b=(2m​). Thus the identity holds as a polynomial identity, even at repeated coordinates. At shifted partition coordinates with t=−1, it proves the removable-corner recurrence in the hook-length formula.

The coefficient is the product of their two Vandermonde determinants divided by the factorial product. Ratios of such alternants yield the Weyl dimension formula by taking a torus character to the identity.

Zero power sums force a finite complex multiset to vanish (∑j=1n​λjk​=0 (1≤k≤n) ⟹ λj​=0)
Words: 69
Vandermonde matrix OurBigBook.com
Collect the distinct nonzero values among the λj​ as μ1​,…,μr​ with positive multiplicities mj​. The first r power sums imply ∑j​mj​μjk​=0 for 1≤k≤r. The coefficient matrix is an invertible weighted Vandermonde matrix, so all mj​ vanish, a contradiction unless r=0. Its invertibility also follows because a polynomial ∑k=1r​ak​zk vanishing at zero and all the μj​ has r+1 distinct roots and degree at most r.

r=x12​x2​+x22​x3​+x32​x1​,s=x22​x1​+x32​x2​+x12​x3​

Artin-Schreier embedding problems over a characteristic-p field

Words: 99
Artin–Schreier theory OurBigBook.com
For a field F of characteristic p, the exact sequence 0→Fp​→Fsepz↦zp−z​Fsep→0, together with additive normal-basis acyclicity, gives H2(Gal(Fsep/F),Fp​)=0. Consequently every central finite embedding problem with group homomorphism kernel Cp​ has a continuous weak solution: its pulled-back two-cocycle is a coboundary, whose correcting one-cochain supplies the lift. Over Fp​((t)), independent Artin–Schreier classes t−m, with m>0 prime to p, allow the lift to be twisted by characters so that inertia maps onto the group homomorphism kernel as well as onto the original quotient. Induction through central order-p quotients therefore realizes every finite p-group as the Galois group of a totally ramified extension with residue field Fp​.
